paper_paragraphs: The external test uses BIM-Edit/BIM-Edit pinned to commit 0ae510bd21865def4e2c6145c1244f01a1e3bcb9. Task variants are deduplicated by input/reference pair. A metadata-only limit of 25,000,000 bytes per file, fixed before outcomes, selects 36 of 54 unique realistic pairs (12 each for creation, update and deletion), involving 43 distinct IFC files; 18 exclusions are recorded. Of these, 36 pairs completed, with operation counts {'create': 12, 'update': 12, 'delete': 12}. The completed input files contain 5 distinct IfcBuilding identifiers; edit pairs and files are not independent buildings.

Geometry extraction completed for 43 of 43 selected files, yielding 25,524 fingerprints from 25,736 IfcElement/IfcSpace instances summed across distinct files; 212 instances have no usable geometry. Unique common object GlobalIds give partial reference correspondences only. Object GlobalIds and Tags are masked in method inputs; class, name, geometry and container identifiers remain available, including stable contextual information. Predictions involving neither reference-labelled side are unadjudicated. Missing geometry, duplicate IDs, target availability and per-pair scores are retained. The benchmark authors describe human-authored IFC edits; these are not consecutive operational MEP histories.

Across completed pairs, original-hybrid macro-average precision/recall are 100.00%/99.65%, compared with 100.00%/97.90% for the review matcher. On reference-labelled update targets, the original hybrid recovers 4/12, and the review matcher recovers 6/12. All 12 requested update targets have available geometry and unique common reference identifiers. These targeted results limit any interpretation of high all-element scores as successful handling of redesign. No parameter fitting uses the external data.

For the review matcher, 0/12 new reference entities are linked to an old object, and 0/12 reference-deleted targets are carried forward. These are operation-specific diagnostics with available geometric labels; they do not establish correctness for unlabelled replacements. The original hybrid counts are 0/12 and 0/12, respectively.

A target-level cost audit shows that all six update targets missed by the review matcher have true-pair costs above the fixed 0.5 m gate, with centre displacements from 0.8 to 3.9 m. This is a demonstrated scope limit of the gate; it was not loosened after observing these outcomes. Placement recovers 8/12 changed targets but falsely carries 5/12 deleted targets and links 5/12 created entities. The zero-gap and 0.03 m review variants give the same external outcomes, so this subset provides no separate empirical benefit for the additional margin.
